notes:
Summary:
- Mid-market product analytics SaaS; embedding-powered product search + chat support for power users.  
- Currently using a mix of managed API calls to public models; evaluating Redwood for predictable latency and cost.

Timeline / recent activity:
- 2026-01-25: Intro call (Avery + Ravi). High-level requirements captured; demo requested. (Fireflies ff-5538-phaedra-2026-01-28).
- 2026-01-28: Hosted API demo: walked through streaming, tool-calls, per-token cost. Team liked transparent perf profiles.
- 2026-02-02: Follow-up call with infra lead (K. Morales) — asked about VPC/private-control-plane options and KMS integration.
- 2026-02-05: Scoped 2-week Hosted POC: 3 flows (chat support, embeddings reindex, reranking experiment). AE sent pricing deck (drive:/decks/phaedra-redwood-pricing-v2.pptx).
- 2026-02-08: Pre-POC sync: security team sent initial questionnaire (drive:/security/phaedra-security-responses.docx). SE to propose Dedicated sizing if Hosted POC shows latency/throughput requirements.

Requirements / constraints (from calls):
- Workloads: chat (latency-target 150-300ms p50 for short contexts), embeddings (bulk offline + nearline batch), reranking (tight tail latency).
- Throughput: moderate peak traffic; expect spikes during product events. Need predictable tail latency.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-high — wants clear unit economics per query. CTO: "We need to know cost/token at scale, not a black box."
- Model preferences: open-model-first; willing to use quantized variants if quality preserved. Wants routing/fallback to cheaper model when latency spike or cost budget hit.
- Security: SSO/SAML, SOC2 compliance, audit logs, customer-managed KMS, and US-only data residency for some datasets.

POC & evaluation plan:
- Phase 1 (Hosted POC - 2 weeks): integrate chat API for support flows, run embeddings pipeline on sample corpus, run reranking A/B. Measure latency, cost, and quality.
- Phase 2 (Cost-Opt Workshop): 90-minute workshop with Redwood SE + product team to present batching/caching strategies, quantization profile tradeoffs, and a unit-economics model tuned to Phaedra's traffic shape. Deliverable: expected $/active-user and recommended config (batch sizes, cache rules, quant profiles).
- Phase 3 (Dedicated sizing): if POC shows >X qps or security needs, produce Dedicated capacity estimate + reserved pricing.

Key technical asks for workshop/proposal:
- Historical traffic shape template from Phaedra to model batching impact.
- Examples of prefix / KV caching rules for chat sessions.
- Benchmarks of quantized model variants vs fp16 on latency and quality for their reranking flow.
- Clear fallback policy examples (route to smaller model, degrade noncritical features).

Quotes / call notes:
- "We need predictable unit economics — show me batching + cache math." — CTO L. Mercer.
- "If dedicated reduces 40% cost at our volume we can commit to reserved capacity" — Finance lead (VP Ops).

Open questions / blockers:
- Security team needs specific KMS/HSM integration details (SEC-4478).
- Data residency: which logs are allowed to leave AWS region? Need legal signoff.
- Budget committee: want committed ARR bands and breakpoints tied to unit-cost targets.

Next steps (short):
- Confirm dates for Cost-Opt Workshop (target week of 2026-02-15).
- Provide traffic sample template to Phaedra infra (by 2026-02-12).
- SE to prepare quantization + batching slides and run quick perf tests for reranking sample.

Attachments / references: pricing deck (drive:/decks/phaedra-redwood-pricing-v2.pptx), security responses (drive:/security/phaedra-security-responses.docx), Fireflies meeting id ff-5538-phaedra-2026-01-28.
